newsitem.title: UK: BA cabin crew vote for three-day strikes.
newsitem.headline: BA cabin crew vote for three-day strikes.

text.p: British Airways cabin crew workers Monday night voted in favour of a series of three-day strikes in their 5-month-old dispute over pay and conditions.

The result of the vote, held at a meeting between cabin crew workers and their union, the Transport and General Workers Union at London's Heathrow airport, will be submitted Tuesday to the union's general secretary, Bill Morris, for approval.

"The meeting made a recommendation that they go for a series of 72-hour disputes (strikes). That will be relayed to General Secretary Bill Morris who will authorise it," union spokesman George Ryde told reporters.
If Morris approves the action, he will set the date for the first strike, Ryde said.

Cabin crew workers voted by a margin of two-to-one last week in favour of strikes, while the airline's ground staff voted earlier Monday to hold a separate strike to protest British Airway's planned sale of its catering unit.

The threatened strikes have made it likely that British Airways flights will be seriously disrupted. However, Morris has written to the airline's chief executive, Robert Ayling, offering peace talks in the dispute with the ground staff.
British Airways is trying to save 1 billion pounds ($1.7 billion) by 2000 in a cost-cutting drive, and the squeeze has put it into conflict with the unions.
